title: Withdrawal rate: how long the money may last
objectives: Calculate a withdrawal rate and read the illustration table.
Explain why a small rate change makes a big difference.
body_md:
Building a corpus is half the job. Drawing it down so it lasts, through inflation and market falls, is the other half. Withdrawal rate = first year's withdrawal ÷ corpus. ₹4 L a year from ₹1 Cr is a 4% withdrawal rate. Illustration: how long ₹1 Cr may last (withdrawal rises 6% a year for inflation; portfolio earns an assumed 9% a year, steadily).

| First-year withdrawal | Withdrawal rate | Approximate years it lasts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ₹3 L | 3% | 50+ years |
| ₹4 L | 4% | ≈ 41 years |
| ₹5 L | 5% | ≈ 28 years |
| ₹6 L | 6% | ≈ 21 years |
| ₹7 L | 7% | ≈ 17 years |

A small change in the withdrawal rate makes a big difference to how long the money lasts. Real markets are not steady, so real outcomes will differ.
example: ₹4 L from ₹1 Cr = 4% → ≈ 41 years (illustrative, 9% assumed, 6% inflation). ₹6 L from ₹1 Cr = 6% → ≈ 21 years.
say: Withdrawal rate = first year's withdrawal ÷ corpus.
A small rate change makes a big difference.
never: The withdrawal rate is the return divided by the corpus.

check.q: How is the withdrawal rate calculated?
check.why: First year’s withdrawal ÷ corpus. ₹4 L from ₹1 Cr is 4%.

check.q: In the illustration, about how long does ₹1 Cr last at a 4% rate?

check.why: 21 years. Going from 4% to 6% roughly halves it.
